artifacts.synopsis: Mrs. Plowman was suspended from the Lord's Table and found guilty of contumacy by the Session of Lehigh Valley Presbyterian Church after refusing to compel her minor daughters to testify; her subsequent appeal was informally rejected by the chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee, who advised her to refile as a complaint. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that Mrs. Plowman had submitted to regular trial and had a right to appeal, and remanded the case to Philadelphia Presbytery for adjudication.

artifacts.title: Stated supply's role as session moderator and congregational meeting chair

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that a stated supply becomes moderator only by session invitation or presbytery appointment, and a session member, not the stated supply, should open congregational meetings.

artifacts.title: Session member serving as moderator in judicial cases

matches.evidence: The CCB found an overture allowing a session to elect one of its own members as moderator in judicial cases to be not in conflict with the BCO.

artifacts.title: Relationship of assistant pastor to congregation under BCO 22

matches.evidence: An overture detailing how assistant pastors are called was found in conflict with BCO 3-2 and 12-2 through 12-4, as the relationship of an assistant pastor to a congregation is best left to the session.
